summary: The proposal is a valid unapproved documentation/metadata pilot, not an execution packet. Self-review correctly narrowed several original overclaims (R4 deep-interview, R8 mass root rewrite, R9 identical-block deletion, S8 test-cadence cut, static-size-as-cost, session-equals-resolver, inline-relabel of a cheaper executor) and correctly added R15. D1–D12 stay outside the executor envelope, and the plan does not recommend dropping independent review, audit-implementation, full release validation, post-commit checks, all-host install proof, or live post-deploy evidence. I do not rubber-stamp S10 as a real authority contradiction: autorun ‘P0 decides’ is the owner stop, not a license to skip SEV-1/2 checkpoints. The first slice is not ready to authorize execute-changeset. P1 does not freeze description-level safety/opt-in/exclusion clauses before a cheaper model may classify them as movable ‘procedural narration.’ P2’s AC4 (‘one unambiguous continuation contract’) contradicts its own conflict-parking rule and can leave the weaker always-TaskUpdate block first. Later handoff still allows mode=inline when a different cheaper model implements, which is the S6/D8 failure mode. P2 substantive SKILL.md edits can arm validate-skill-before-starting.sh and force out-of-envelope procedure, and the skill-judgment validator script itself is inside the write envelope.

findings.claim: P1 tells a cheaper executor to move ‘procedural narration’ out of descriptions without a frozen inventory of trigger, exclusion, opt-in, and approval-boundary clauses, so safety-bearing routing text can leave the always-visible description.
findings.analysis: AC2 requires preserving every positive condition, automatic lane condition, exclusion, and approval boundary. P1 simultaneously orders the implementer to ‘Move provider/receipt detail, history and procedural narration into the corresponding existing body section.’ Several of the twelve descriptions mix applicability with load-bearing gates that a host or cheap router sees only in frontmatter: plan-blast-radius states SEV-1/2 force human_checkpoint regardless of autorun; blind-control-plan is WARN/shadow default OFF unless dual-track is armed; craft-prompt says it does NOT route svc work; evaluate-rule says always use before registering a rule; review-exec states same-family Sol is advisory and the configured different-family station owns independent release authority. Those are invocation prerequisites/exclusions, not beat-sheet or provider inventory. The promised before/after map is an output, so an executor can rationalize dropped phrases after the edit. Original R5 was about truncation hiding Use-when; the fix is to keep the selection and stop conditions at the front, not to relocate them. Self-review SR-04 already warned that frontmatter trigger edits are behavioral; this slice still lacks a mechanical preserve-list.

findings.proposed_fix: Before any P1 edit, freeze a per-skill clause inventory from baseline e50a6443: explicit requests, automatic conditions, exclusions, default-OFF/opt-in, owner/SEV/approval boundaries, and specialist non-overlap lines. Require the new description to contain every inventory item verbatim (or a recorded equivalent that does not drop meaning). Classify SEV checkpoints, default-OFF, ‘does not route’, independent-review authority, and ‘always use before registering’ as description-level prerequisites, not movable procedural narration. Treat the before/after map as proof against that inventory, not as a substitute for it. Do not change generic false-positive triggers (R2/D1) while frontloading.

findings.claim: P2’s success criterion AC4 requires one unambiguous continuation contract, but the process parks material conflicts and can leave the weaker ‘always TaskUpdate’ instruction as the first block a cheaper executor follows.
findings.analysis: analyze-domain, evaluate-rule, and sync-work-items each repeat ‘Task-graph mode’ three times. The first block tells Claude Code to mirror with TaskList/TaskUpdate. The second block restricts mirroring to the parent session, forbids subagent TaskUpdate, and is the canonical child-containment rule. Those are not duplicate equivalent obligations (self-review SR-01). P2 says keep the union of non-conflicting obligations and, if blocks conflict materially, leave the disputed lines for D2/D3 rather than inventing policy. D2 is completion vs approval; D3 is relevant reads. Host-mirroring/subagent TaskUpdate is authority/containment (S4/D7). AC4 still requires ‘each pilot skill has one unambiguous local continuation contract.’ Parking both conflicting lines fails AC4; unioning them without a winner also fails AC4; deleting the stronger parent-only rule would weaken AGENTS.md child containment. A cheaper isolated executor that stops at the first ‘Task-graph mode’ heading will emit TaskUpdate from a child. That is execute-risk, not a documentation nit.

findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite AC4 to a mechanically testable predicate. Either (a) keep the already-canonical stronger parent-only / no-subagent-TaskUpdate rule (AGENTS.md child containment and the second local block) and record the weaker first-block ‘always mirror’ line as superseded local drift — this is alignment to existing authority, not a new policy — or (b) do not claim unambiguity: leave both lines, list the conflict under D7, and change AC4 to ‘no unique obligation dropped; remaining conflicts enumerated and not silently resolved.’ Never park this under D2/D3. Proof is one remaining local continuation block plus a conflict ledger, not a regex collapse.

findings.claim: The intended Astra-plans / cheaper-model-implements split is stated, but the future implementation mode is not pinned, so a later handoff can still label a different executor `inline` and skip dispatch blueprints.
findings.analysis: plan-changeset makes §3a mandatory on dispatch, skips blueprints only when the same orchestrator applies the change with context already loaded, and fail-closes unmarked mode to dispatch. Original S6 and self-review SR-07 / D8 correctly forbid relabeling a separate cheaper executor as inline. This document says it is not yet a certified inline-v4 or legacy-dispatch receipt and that CREATE/MODIFY should be frozen later using ‘the selected executor's supported plan-manifest contract.’ That leaves the mode choice open at the exact moment a cheaper model would implement P1–P4. Description/continuation/prose edits look tempting to mark inline because ‘the planner already has context.’ If the implementer is not that planner, blueprints are the cheaper model’s contract. Priority (5) of this review is exactly that misuse. The current planning request need not include blueprints; it must not leave a hole that drops them at execute authorization.

findings.claim: The pilot write envelope includes validate-skill-judgment.mjs, so a cheaper executor can change matcher logic until frontloaded descriptions pass instead of adding failing-then-passing fixtures.
findings.analysis: P1’s proof is parsed description and routing behavior, not character length. That is the right class of proof. The Files Planned list allows edits to the existing validator script and its behavior.json ‘only when applicable counterexamples are needed.’ Counterexamples belong in fixtures. Editing the matcher can hide a lost exclusion or a newly gained generic trigger (exactly AC2’s risk). That weakens the cheaper-executor and review contract the way a provider-fidelity test that only asserts success would. The plan’s ‘no new always-on checklist’ rule does not prevent loosening the existing one.

findings.claim: P3 both forbids changing generated mirrors by hand and allows running the existing generator, whose outputs are not in the stated write envelope.
findings.analysis: P3’s named files are CLAUDE.md, plan-changeset/SKILL.md, execute-changeset/SKILL.md, references/model-routing.md, and rules/common/model-selection.md. CLAUDE.md contains svc:generated model tables. The plan says do not overwrite generated mirror blocks manually: use the existing generator or leave a labelled registry-default table intact. The generator, if run from a model-routing source correction, typically refreshes multiple host entry files (not only CLAUDE.md). Those files are absent from ‘the union of P1’s twelve, P2’s three, and P3’s five.’ An implementer who runs the generator either leaks the envelope or ships a partial mirror set. An implementer who hand-edits the generated table violates P3. This is an unresolved consequential execute choice (rubric point 10) inside an otherwise correct ‘no policy/registry pin change’ constraint.

findings.claim: P1 applies description frontloading to all twelve over-600 skills, including review-plan, review-exec, and research, which is larger than the minimum viable proof and puts chain-gate routing metadata in the first cheaper-executor batch.
findings.analysis: The original recommendation was to start with trigger precision and duplicate removal. Self-review SR-11 narrowed large-root/mode work to a three-skill continuation pilot; P2 follows that. P1 does not stage the same way: it includes the two G5/G4-adjacent review gates and research, whose descriptions carry independent-review topology, promotion blocking, and uncertainty-triggered invocation. The frontload mechanic is already fully present in ad-video-script (procedure before Use-when ~character 639), design-logo, align-feature, and analyze-marketing. Those four would prove clause preservation and routing-index regeneration without touching gate selection text. Including review-plan/review-exec in the same serial batch means a P1 mistake blocks P2/P3 and can alter when mandatory chain skills are offered. Census membership of the twelve is also unverified here because inventory.json was not in the review pack (see dependencies_needing_read).

findings.claim: Self-review and D7 treat autorun ‘P0 decides’ versus plan-blast-radius ‘HUMAN CHECKPOINT REQUIRED’ as a contradictory authority hole; the supplied autorun rows present P0 as the owner stop, so a later ‘correction’ could add churn or a second stop without relaxing or strengthening anything.
findings.analysis: This is a self-review challenge, not a first-slice defect. plan-blast-radius body requires a human checkpoint for SEV-1/2 regardless of autorun. The autorun table says stop, ask the user to approve SEV classification, P0 decides, and calls classification deterministic. Other autorun rows use P0 as the human operator (‘P0 merges’, ‘P0 reviews diffs’). If P0 is the owner, the table already implements the skill’s hard stop. Original S10’s ‘potential unauthorized destructive execution’ overstated the conflict unless a definition of P0 as the autonomous agent exists outside the supplied excerpt. D7 is unapproved and says ‘No new mutation permission,’ which is the right boundary; it should not instruct an executor to ‘correct the autorun table’ as if SEV approval were currently missing. I accept S4, S11, and S12 as real stale-prose/authority issues; I reject S10 as confirmed contradiction on this evidence.
